cohort: 100 individuals aged 6-16 years old, divided into two groups: 50 with mandibular asymmetry and 50 without
finding: Male gender, oral ventilation, short-term vaginal nasalization, dental trauma, and visual disorders were associated with mandibular asymmetry, while asthma, prematurity, and cesarean section were not.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was not found to be associated with mandibular asymmetry, potentially due to the absence of trauma during delivery.
